payload.entry: The epic lander for this epic should create a new epic but let's stop it at two rounds. Make sure the epic lander for the next epic is aware of this stop point.

CHECK-FULL VERIFICATION AND CALIBRATION (2026-11-27)

The new isolated full-run evidence is attached: file:explicit:0c6bf85783f13300e8d3c47c (4,301,960-byte raw recording) and file:explicit:1fa482f4cf347ac59b28ab35 (complete 144,447-byte monitor log). Monitor 62r1026bwztg ran the exact four-worker `just check-full` command from 19:13:59Z to 21:00:43Z and exited 1 after the complete pytest lane. It selected 63,822 fast-suite nodes over 5,847 files. All four workers reported; their per-worker node totals sum to 63,822. No worker crashed or stopped early. No ad-hoc paths, shards, `-k`, or non-default marker selection were used; the default fast lane excludes slow and visual tests by design.

The global leak detector reported four ACE tests poisoning `sase.config.core._live_config_token_refresh_threads`; the baseline independently confirmed `tests/ace/tui/test_agent_jump_clan_members.py::test_real_app_named_agent_jump_expands_collapsed_clan` on the same global. Existing owner `sase-1vg` remains open and covers this signature. `check-full` stopped in test-cost before visual snapshots; no visual report or PNG golden change was produced.

The recording replay initially found one local hard miss: collection CPU 53.562 seconds per worker exceeded the old 51.25 effective limit. CI replay passed. The isolated `--suggest` output recommends 51.0 using `round_up_nice(53.562 / (0.85 * 1.25))`; that committed hard limit leaves 16.0% sample headroom under its 63.75 effective allowance. After the update, both local and CI replays pass. Advisory wall overages were left advisory. Compared with the earlier same-day 4-worker sample, total file CPU rose 5.1%; per-cause CPU changes were 2.7-8.8%, and the largest current file was 1.88% of total CPU, so the measurements support suite-wide growth without a named per-file regression. Collection CPU has no per-file attribution.

Focused budget, runner, and Telemetry workflow contracts passed (93 tests). `sase tool run check` 533ceda265c79af4d7f890c0177218bd passed, including all static gates and scoped tests. `sase bead epic-symbols sase-1vn.2` returned no entries. Closing this phase with the independently tracked leak-gate exception preserved above; the parent epic remains open.

payload.entry: CHILD LANDING BLOCKER: sase-1vn.3.1 verification found three remaining host acceptance gaps: failed resource cleanup is falsely recorded complete and not retried; same-origin staging can overwrite saved failed-stage evidence; normal failure settlement runs before terminal evidence and has no post-terminal retry. Both child phase check receipts are green and 86 targeted Python tests pass, but isolated probes expose these omissions. A medium tale authored by the child lander will fix only the remaining work, reverify integration, close sase-1vn.3.1 and mark its linked plan done, then verify and close this parent phase normally. Leave containing epic sase-1vn to its waiting land agent. No new unrelated task proposals; separate sase-1r4/1si/1sj scopes remain untouched.

Verified failed-turn-handoffs scope after child epic sase-1vn.3.1 closeout. Child plan plan:202611/failed_turn_handoffs.md is status: done. Epic-symbol audit for sase-1vn.3 returned no entries. Reviewer decisions remain cost_budgets=rebaseline and zombie_recovery=relaunch; this phase did not change them.

A never-started staged handoff whose originating turn failed no longer counts as live ownership: incomplete cleanup stays retryable, the origin's saved stage is preserved against same-turn overwrite, and settlement runs after durable failed done.json. Later-turn questions use a fresh artifacts dir. Explicit readopt still requires authenticated finalizer proof and does not auto-adopt.

sase tool run check 3b04501a99aa2f3dbd52fb4330c74021 succeeded; 36 inactive-host tests passed; just symvision clean. Containing epic sase-1vn and plan:202611/backlog_epic_1.md stay with the waiting land agent. sase-1sh is not closed here: live origin 3w69pb9ezmfy has no durable failed done.json (origin_not_failed), so settlement is correctly withheld; the land agent has the inspect recommendation on sase-1vn.3.1 note #3.

Reporting phase live inventory (2026-11-28T03:12Z, core pin 91380657): sase bead zombies on the canonical sase store reports 33 zombie(s), 6 unknown, 2 owned, 90 not-zombie. Examples sase-zu and sase-zn are both still zombies (all descendants closed, child_landed, recovery eligible). Full report: file:explicit:95fcc65660f2a5ea7525e495. No bead was armed, claimed, launched, closed, or reopened.

Zombie liveness phase evidence: read-only all-project report file:explicit:2195f969cb91f0108061888d (generated 2026-11-28T06:37:17Z) covered 11 projects and 162 plans: 38 recovery-eligible zombies, 2 owned, 15 unknown, 107 not zombies. The roost project store was not materialized and is recorded as a collection failure; all other project reports loaded. No historical bead rows were modified.

PHASE VERIFIED by the sase-1vn.4.1 land agent. Child epic sase-1vn.4.1 completes this phase's scope. Detect: the shared core predicate needs an in_progress plan, a complete descendant tree with every descendant closed, and no session owner. Report: sase bead zombies (compact/json, -a) plus the TUI stranded badge; live inventories are attached here. Recover per zombie_recovery=relaunch: the epic_liveness AXE job relaunches only the land agent through a durable, guarded proc. sase-1vn.4.1 closes through host completion after its landing commit, and that close cascade-closes this phase (delegated work landed). Tested invariants for the outer land agent: (a) arming is report-only, and closes at or before the cutoff stay historical; (b) one claim per (project, epic, close-event token), created only if absent and published before launch; a losing or foreign host never launches and claims are never transferred; (c) proc id and fingerprint are deterministic per claim, so crash replay resumes the same request and a terminal proc stays consumed (no relaunch); (d) a close-token guard at launch_epic_bead_work aborts if a child reopened, an owner appeared, or the token changed, so recovery never launches phase workers; (e) 120s settlement grace, 30s budget, at most 1 submission per pass across all projects, fair restart-safe cursors; (f) unknown evidence, non-epic tiers, and owned plans are report-only; (g) nothing closes a plan bead automatically. No recovery proc has run (sase proc list -a -t epic-recovery is empty). Not closed per plan: sase-1vn and sase-12u; the evidence above is for the outer land agent's triage of sase-12u. Follow-ups filed: sase-1vv (sase-core query_cache timing flake), sase-1vw (admission overlap flake), sase-1vx (countdown-tick GC flake); the refresh_warmup_gc flake is already owned by sase-1v2.

- sase-1un: closed by sase-1vn.1.
- sase-j0: closed now (done). The CI Telemetry recording from run 46071761552 replays green with --ci, and the test-cost job finishes in 2:03 inside its 180m cap. The remaining red is the leak gate owned by sase-1vg; evidence was noted there.
